Events were sampled probabilistically according to NIST XCOM mass attenuation coefficients for liquid water at 2.0 MeV. Compton scattering angles were drawn from the Klein-Nishina differential cross section using rejection sampling; photoelectric electrons were assigned forward-peaked angles; Rayleigh scattering was simulated with exponentially distributed small-angle kicks; pair production kinematics split kinetic energy symmetrically with forward emission. All values adhere to energy-momentum conservation and physical thresholds.
